answer: In an economy of AI agents, the use of cryptographic hash functions enables Sybil resistance through mechanisms like Merkle trees. By aggregating agent identities into a single, publicly verifiable signal, malicious agents attempting to create fake identities risk being identified as a whisper of anomalies in the aggregate. If an attacker accumulates too many conflicting identities, their attempts are akin to trying to fan the flames of a dying ember, ultimately leading to their own exposure and expulsion from the network.
